subject: Late-stage slab allocation & fallback mapping — Nebula Dynamics
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Smith <julia.smith@nebuladynamics.com>, procurement@nebuladynamics.com
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Late-stage slab allocation & fallback mapping — Nebula Dynamics

Team,

Nebula Dynamics (NDX) verbally signaled commitment this week pending a capacity assurance for Q3 ramp. They want a firm, short-term hold on a "slab" of dedicated capacity while they finalize procurement paperwork. Julia included here is the buyer.

I need an internal availability check + recommendation by EOD today. Specifically:
- Inventory: how many A100-80GB-equivalent slots (or equivalent vCPU/GPU mix) can we soft-hold in us-west for the 90-day window starting 2027-07-01?
- Shape: propose 2 sizing options — a "baseline" (predictable daily throughput) and a "burstable" slab (adds queued capacity during spikes).
- Fallbacks: if we can't fully reserve, what partial mappings (mixed quantized instances, lower memory variants) can keep the deal within SLA targets?
- Ops runbook steps to convert a soft-hold to a hard allocation (who signs off, lead times, cost uplift).

Attached: nebula_capacity_request.xlsx with NDX’s expected token volume and runtime profile. HubSpot link (below) has contract draft.

Can each of you flag blocker items in your area (thermal/runway, pricing delta, SLA exceptions)? Julia — if you can confirm the target start date is still 2027-07-01 and whether finance needs a PO by May 10 that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Sofia

--
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0128

Attachments: nebula_capacity_request.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB); ndx-service-sla-draft.pdf (pdf, 38KB)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Smith <julia.smith@nebuladynamics.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-stage slab allocation & fallback mapping — Nebula Dynamics

Sofia —

Quick inventory snapshot from the pool manager:
- us-west dedicated pool A: 24 A100-80GB-equivalent slots free today.
- us-west nodal reserve (short-term): 8 slots can be placed in soft-hold for up to 45 days without impacting existing commitments; beyond that we need signed reserved capacity.

Sizing options (high level):
1) Baseline slab:
   - 12 x A100-80GB (stable throughput). Expected latency SLOs unchanged.
   - Estimated commit lead-time to hard allocation: 14 days.
2) Burstable slab:
   - 8 x A100 + 8 x T4-quantized burst nodes (cost-effective for daytime spikes).
   - Needs prefix cache tuning; possible 5-8% throughput variance.

Fallbacks/mapping:
- If we can't dedicate full A100s, we can map 6 A100 + 12 quantized 4-bit instances with KV cache warmers; this preserves prompt latency for 85% of traffic.
- Cross-region fallback (us-east) available with 35–45ms added median RTT — only suitable if NDX accepts slightly higher latency for non-critical batches.

Ops runbook notes: soft-hold -> hard allocation requires: product ops ticket -> infra lead sign-off (Karthik) -> finance PO -> capacity activation window (14d). I attached the quick steps in the internal runbook link.

Blocking items:
- Thermal headroom for a 12-slot hard allocation in us-west on the proposed cluster is marginal; we'd need to carve from pool A and possibly move two evaporated nodes to the reserve pool.
- Pricing: burstable slab increases unit cost by ~12% given mixed hardware; finance should confirm acceptable uplift.

I'll hold 6 slots in soft-hold (internal tag: SLAB-NDX-0701) for 48 hours to buy time. If procurement needs a longer soft-hold we should raise to leadership for exception.

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Head of Dedicated Sizing, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Smith <julia.smith@nebuladynamics.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-stage slab allocation & fallback mapping — Nebula Dynamics

Thanks for the inventory callout Karthik. A couple of commercial/ops points from my side: 

1) Impact on pipeline: carving 12 A100 eq for NDX in us-west over July–Sept would overlap with two late-stage opportunities (see internal ticket: OPS-4721). If we commit without signed terms we risk a scramble in June.

2) Recommendation: propose a hybrid contractual approach to NDX — a 6-slot hard commit + 6-slot burstable option that converts to hard if they hit the Q3 thresholds. This reduces our runway risk and gives them a path to scale.

3) Paperwork: if NDX can sign a Letter of Intent (LoI) with a short 30% non-refundable hold fee, Finance can provisionally earmark the other 6 slots as a contingent reserve. I'll loop in Finance if Julia confirms willingness.

Sofia — if you can get a LoI or a PO by May 10, we can push the hard-commit conversion without disrupting the rest of the pipeline. Otherwise we should limit us-west hard holds to the 6 slots Karthik placed.

Marcus

--
Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Solutions & Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Julia Smith <julia.smith@nebuladynamics.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 14:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Late-stage slab allocation & fallback mapping — Nebula Dynamics

Sofia / team —

Thanks for the quick responses and for placing an initial soft hold. Confirming: NDX is comfortable with the hybrid approach Marcus proposed. We can sign an LoI with a 30% holding fee and aim to deliver a PO by May 7. Our target start for production capacity remains 2027-07-01; we need at least 6 hard slots guaranteed by June 15.

A few clarifying items:
- Can you provide the expected cost delta for the hybrid (6 hard + 6 burstable) vs full 12 hard? A simple table would help procurement.
- We also need an escalation contact if thermal or provisioning delays occur during activation.

Sofia — I'll upload a draft LoI to the HubSpot record this afternoon. Procurement copied here (procurement@nebuladynamics.com) will coordinate the PO.

Best,
Julia

Procurement contact: procurement@nebuladynamics.com
